caption: Newanforbi v. United Parcel Service, Inc.
claims: PC §290.46(j)(2)(E) Violation, Failure to Hire (Tameny), ICRAA, Invasion of Privacy, Negligence Per Se, UCL §17200
status: Filed July 15, 2026 — limitations preserved 16 days ahead of the July 31, 2026 cutoff (Dept. 11B, Hon. Robert T. Waters; CMC Jan. 13, 2027). Served July 22, 2026 on UPS via CSC; responsive pleading due Aug. 21, 2026. Amended CCP §425.115 notice ($250,000) executed and signed Aug. 17, 2026 — not yet filed or served.
defendants: United Parcel Service, Inc.; and DOES 1 through 10, inclusive
causes: Failure to Hire in Violation of Public Policy (Tameny)
Violation of ICRAA (Cal. Civ. Code § 1786 et seq.)
Invasion of Privacy (Cal. Const., Art. I, § 1)
Unlawful Business Practices (Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200 et seq.)
key_facts: In or around mid-2024, Plaintiff applied for a position in UPS's delivery and logistics operations in California. As part of its standard pre-employment screening, UPS initiated a background check through First Advantage (fadv.com). On July 22, 2024 at 9:57 AM, Plaintiff received a 'Pre Adverse Action Notification regarding your application with UPS' from First Advantage (DoNotReply@fadv.com) directing him to review the report for 'UNITED PARCEL SERVICE' via a secure portal link. Reminder notices followed on July 23, 2024 (10:00 AM) and July 27, 2024 (10:00 AM). On July 31, 2024 at 9:57 AM — nine days after the original pre-adverse notice — Plaintiff received a 'Final Adverse Action Notification regarding your application with UPS,' confirming UPS had taken final adverse action, definitively denying him employment. UPS provided no written communication identifying any basis for the denial other than the background screening report; no other disqualifying information existed in Plaintiff's application. Plaintiff is a registrant on California's Megan's Law sex offender registry, and alleges on information and belief that the First Advantage report disclosed that status to UPS (together with a statutory disclaimer warning that the information could not lawfully be used for employment purposes) and that UPS used it as the basis for the denial, in violation of Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E).
procedural_status: Pre-filing demand July 12, 2026 ($85,000; deadline July 26). Complaint filed July 15, 2026 (STK-CV-UWT-2026-0009113); FW-003 granted. As with Matter 25, the First Advantage report is unavailable — registry use pled on information and belief. Served July 22, 2026 via Sacramento County Sheriff on Josh Swindell / CSC; POS-010 mailed to court July 28, 2026. Responsive pleading due Aug. 21, 2026 (meet-and-confer by ~Aug. 14 if demurrer). Amended §425.115 ($250,000) executed and signed Aug. 17, 2026, superseding the Aug. 4 $25,000 placeholder and the unsigned Aug. 7 generated original — not yet filed or served. Same-day/same-court filing as Matter 25; CRC 3.300 notice unlikely. Dated service/deadline beats live in timeline.json.
damages: Statutory civil remedy under PC § 290.46(j)(4)(A): actual damages or $25,000, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees, for each unlawful use of registry information. CONSERVATIVE: ~$33,000 (statutory minimum plus modest emotional distress; no wage documentation on file, since Plaintiff never began working for UPS). MODERATE: ~$85,000 (statutory penalty, ICRAA punitive damages up to $5,000 for willful noncompliance, emotional distress, and partial fee-shifting). AGGRESSIVE: ~$200,000 (aggregation across all six causes of action plus Civil Code § 3294 punitive damages, if discovery yields the actual First Advantage report and confirms willful registry-based denial). As with Matter 25, there are no lost W-2 wages to claim — the primary economic recovery theory is the statutory penalty and lost opportunity/career-advancement damages.
risk: Favorable on the law (PC § 290.46(j)(2)(E) is categorical and exception-free; negligence per se under Evid. Code § 669) but evidentiarily thinner than Matters 22/23 — UPS never issued a written admission naming the registry as the basis for denial, and the complaint pleads UPS's actual use of registry information 'on information and belief' throughout. The First Advantage notices establish the timeline (application → pre-adverse notice → two reminders → 9-day gap → final adverse action). The limitations risk has been eliminated: the July 15, 2026 filing preserved all time-sensitive claims 16 days before the July 31, 2026 two-year cutoff from the July 31, 2024 adverse action. Discovery (subpoena to First Advantage for the underlying report, or UPS's hiring file) would be needed to convert the information-and-belief pleading to a proven claim. On punitives: the Aug. 17 amended §425.115 ($250,000) sets a default ceiling only — any prove-up award still requires evidence of UPS's financial condition (Adams v. Murakami (1991) 54 Cal.3d 105).
evidence: First Advantage Pre Adverse Action Notification, July 22, 2024, 9:57 AM — background screening report for 'UNITED PARCEL SERVICE'
First Advantage reminder notice, July 23, 2024, 10:00 AM
First Advantage reminder notice, July 27, 2024, 10:00 AM
First Advantage Final Adverse Action Notification, July 31, 2024, 9:57 AM — confirming final denial nine days after pre-adverse notice
California Penal Code § 290.46(j)(1) and (j)(2)(E) — statutory prohibition on registry information use for employment
Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)(3)(A) — pre-adverse action notice requirement
California Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act, Civ. Code § 1786 et seq.
